newsitem.title: POLAND: Isuzu mulls DM 380 mln factory in Poland.
newsitem.headline: Isuzu mulls DM 380 mln factory in Poland.

text.p: Japan's Isuzu is negotiating with authorities in Poland's special economic zone in Katowice, to build a 380 million mark diesel engines factory there, the president of the firm managing the zone said.
Marek Lichon of Katowicka Specjalna Strefa Ekonomiczna SA said Isuzu was likely to decide by the end of November if it would build the factory in the zone.

"Most of the conditions (for building the factory) have already been set and it seems that they (Isuzu) will decide to invest here ... the building and launching of production in means investment of 380 million marks," he told Reuters.
Lichon said the plant, which would employ 400, was expected to have annual sales of 1.1 billion marks.
He said the building of the factory was likely to take two years and Isuzu could start the project in April next year.
He added that the southern town Tychy, near Katowice, were considered as the location for the factory.
Lichon said Isuzu planned later to expand the business by investing further funds but declined to give details.

He said the factory would produce engines for General Motors GM factories in Europe, including the one which GM's subsidiary Adam Opel AG was building in another southern town of Gliwice, also in the special zone.
In Poland's special economic zones investors are exempt from corporate tax, now at 40 percent, for 10 years, and enjoy a 50-percent reduction in the tax during the next 10 years.
